name: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), Business Cycle Dating Committee
description: The committee that dates U.S. business-cycle peaks and troughs. Its chronology, back to December 1854, is the official recession record; FRED's USREC (catalogued as fred/usrec) is the St. Louis Fed's monthly 0/1 interpretation of these dates and is what this site fetches.

notes: The chronology is also a table on the data page and a directory of dated files at https://data.nber.org/cycles/: business_cycle_dates.json (checked 2026-09-14: a list of {peak, trough} month dates starting with the 1854-12-01 trough), US_Business_Cycle_Expansions_and_Contractions.xlsx, BCDC_spreadsheet_for_website.xlsx and dated update folders.
The xlsx path carries a 2023-03 upload date; the file may move when the committee next announces a turning point.

datasets.name: U.S. business cycle expansions and contractions
datasets.gives: Peak and trough months and quarters of U.S. business cycles from the December 1854 peak to the April 2020 trough, with contraction and expansion lengths
notes: Turning points are announced months to a year after they occur, at the committee's discretion, so no fixed lag applies.
Most recent peak February 2020 (2019Q4), most recent trough April 2020 (2020Q2), as shown on 2026-09-14.
Referenced by series/usrec.json as the authority behind FRED's USREC; the fetcher reads USREC, not this file.

datasets.name: NBER Macrohistory Database
datasets.gives: Pre-WWI and interwar era U.S. (with partial U.K., France and Germany coverage) economic series across 16 topic chapters: production and construction, employment, money and banking, prices, asset-market transactions, foreign trade, government activity, and interest rates. Chapter XIII (Interest Rates) alone has ~80 series (78 counted): call money and commercial paper rates, Federal Reserve and foreign central-bank discount rates, open-market rates, corporate/municipal/government bond yields, equity and mortgage yields, and rate spreads; Chapter IV (Prices) has wholesale/retail commodity prices and broad price indices (e.g. BLS wholesale price index, CPI all items). Most series are highly disaggregated and many are US-only.
datasets.units: percent, index points, dollars, varies by series

notes: 16 chapters, each a directory of series files under https://data.nber.org/databases/macrohistory/data/<chapter-number>/ (chapter 13 = interest rates, chapter 04 = prices, etc.); a chapter's own page (e.g. nber.org/research/data/nber-macrohistory-xiii-interest-rates) lists that chapter's series with a series id, date range and cadence.

Series id convention: a one-letter cadence prefix (m = monthly, q = quarterly, a = annual) + two-digit chapter number + three-digit series number, with an optional letter suffix for a revised/alternate vintage of the same underlying series (e.g. m13001 vs m13001a, m13029a vs m13029b).

Each series is offered as a Micro-TSP .db file (data + comment lines together, readable by TSP/Micro-TSP/RATS) and a rectangular .dat file (year/period/value columns, produced from the .db files by Jean Roth in May 2001) plus an accompanying .txt comment file; missing values are 'NA' in .db and '.' in .dat.

A HEAD request on 2026-09-15 to data.nber.org/databases/macrohistory/data/13/m13001a.db returned 200, 9,482 bytes, Last-Modified Fri 2005-08-26 — consistent with a static historical archive, not a series still being extended.

terms.summary: No dataset-specific reuse permission found; the macrohistory database pages carry only the site-wide '© 2026 National Bureau of Economic Research. All Rights Reserved.' footer, not the chronology dataset's explicit 'permission to copy is granted' sentence
terms.quote: © 2026 National Bureau of Economic Research. All Rights Reserved.

notes: Cadence set to 'monthly' as the dominant native cadence within the interest-rate and price chapters checked (most series monthly; a handful quarterly or annual, e.g. q13020 Municipal Bond Yields quarterly, a13049 Earnings Yield annual) rather than 'irregular', since irregular is meant for genuinely event-driven cadence (the chronology dataset), not a mixed-but-mostly-regular one.

Coverage {1824-01, 1972-08} is the outer span actually verified (Chapter XIII's earliest series, Great Britain Open Market Rates of Discount, London (m13016), starts 1824-01; Chapter XIII's latest-ending series, Industrial Bonds Aaa Rating m13026, ends 1972-08). Individual series each cover a narrower window within this; do not treat the whole span as populated for any one series.

Pre-1934 short-rate coverage for chart 5 confirmed directly: Call Money Rates (m13001a) runs 1857-01 through 1934-04, and Commercial Paper Rates NYC (m13002) runs 1857-01 through 1971-12, both spanning the pre-1934 window.

status 'discontinued' is inferred from the 2005 file Last-Modified date and the chapter series' end dates clustering in the 1930s-1970s, plus no discontinuation notice or update log found on any page read — there is no explicit 'this database is no longer updated' statement, only the absence of any newer activity.

'restricted' terms status is a conservative read: 'All Rights Reserved' is NBER's standard site-wide footer (confirmed present on the chronology dataset's own page too, alongside its separate explicit permission sentence), not a macrohistory-specific denial of reuse — but since no permission sentence exists for this dataset the way it does for the chronology, it is not treated as verified/permitted either.

Complementary/successor projects surfaced on the macrohistory page, not catalogued here: the Jordà-Schularick-Taylor Macrohistory Database (macrohistory.net) and the Gordon-Balke American Business Cycle dataset — candidates for their own catalogue files if a future series needs them.
